pins.definition: The external organ of the body used for hearing.
The organ of the body used for hearing.
The organ on the side of the head used for hearing.

situation: An audiologist examines an intricate anatomical model of the human auditory system in a quiet clinic.
subject: the human ear
brief: A detailed 19th-century scientific plate depicts the human external and internal ear in clean ink lines, with delicate cross-sections of the inner structures clearly labeled in fine script against heavy cream paper.
prompt: A detailed 19th-century scientific plate depicts the human external and internal ear in clean ink lines, with delicate cross-sections of the inner structures clearly labeled in fine script against heavy cream paper. a nineteenth-century engraved scientific plate, fine hatching, hand-tinted washes, aged rag paper, the specimen isolated and reverently observed. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
